Answer ALL 10 questions. For your guidance, the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given that $y = \tanh^{-1}\sin x$,

show that

$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \sec x.$$ *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Write $y = \tanh^{-1}(u)$ with $u = \sin x$. The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic tangent is $\dfrac{d}{du}\tanh^{-1}u = \dfrac{1}{1-u^2}$ for $|u|<1$. By the chain rule

$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{1-\sin^2 x}\cdot\frac{d}{dx}(\sin x) = \frac{\cos x}{1-\sin^2 x}.$$

Since $1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x$,

$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{\cos x}{\cos^2 x} = \frac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x. \qquad \blacksquare$$

(Valid where $|\sin x| < 1$, which includes the interval $0 \le x \le \tfrac{\pi}{6}$ used in part (ii).)

**Alternative.** $\tanh^{-1}u = \tfrac12\ln\dfrac{1+u}{1-u}$ gives the same derivative $\dfrac{1}{1-u^2}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Hence, or otherwise, show that

$$\int_0^{\pi/6} \sec^2 x\,\tanh^{-1}\sin x\,dx = \frac{1}{\sqrt3}\left[\sqrt3 - 2 + \frac12\ln 3\right].$$ *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Integration by parts.** Take $u = \tanh^{-1}\sin x$ and $\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \sec^2 x$. Then $\dfrac{du}{dx} = \sec x$ by part (i), and $v = \tan x$. So

$$I = \int_0^{\pi/6}\sec^2 x\,\tanh^{-1}\sin x\,dx = \Big[\tan x\,\tanh^{-1}\sin x\Big]_0^{\pi/6} - \int_0^{\pi/6}\tan x\,\sec x\,dx.$$

**Second integral.** $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sec x) = \sec x\tan x$, so

$$\int_0^{\pi/6}\sec x\tan x\,dx = \Big[\sec x\Big]_0^{\pi/6} = \frac{2}{\sqrt3} - 1,$$

because $\sec\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{1}{\cos(\pi/6)} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}$ and $\sec 0 = 1$.

**Boundary term.** At $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$: $\tan\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$ and $\sin\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac12$, so

$$\tanh^{-1}\tfrac12 = \tfrac12\ln\frac{1+\frac12}{1-\frac12} = \tfrac12\ln 3.$$

The term at $x=0$ is $0$ (since $\tan 0 = 0$). Hence the boundary term is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\cdot\dfrac12\ln 3$.

**Combine.**

$$I = \frac{1}{\sqrt3}\cdot\frac12\ln 3 - \frac{2}{\sqrt3} + 1 = \frac{1}{\sqrt3}\left[\frac12\ln 3 - 2 + \sqrt3\right],$$

using $1 = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{\sqrt3}$. This is

$$\boxed{I = \frac{1}{\sqrt3}\left[\sqrt3 - 2 + \frac12\ln 3\right]} \qquad \blacksquare$$

**Numerical check.** $I \approx 0.16244$ and $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\left(\sqrt3 - 2 + \tfrac12\ln3\right) \approx 0.16244$.
